Hi Elisa — Kimberly here from the infra/security team. Per Marcus's note, I started populating answers to the technical sections of the spreadsheet and attached our mapping (DPF_Mapping_By_Redwood.xlsx). Below are highlights and quick answers to the two clarifying points Marcus raised.

-- Highlights (short):
• EU regions: Our hosted offering runs in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 (redundant). For EU-hosted workloads we segregate control-plane routing so customer requests stay within EU regions unless explicit cross-region features are enabled.
• Cross-border lawful basis: For hosted customers electing EU-region tenancy, we rely on SCCs (EU Commission standard contractual clauses) plus our documented technical and organizational measures linked in the mapping.
• On-prem/Private KMS: We support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) for Private deployments. For hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer KMS via cloud KMS integrations and an option for HSM-backed key wrapping for enterprise customers.

-- Short answers to specific Qs you flagged:
1) EU-residency-only option: Yes — possible via Dedicated/Private deployment. Hosted EU tenancy with SCCs provides strong controls but does mean some infra orchestration metadata may still be logged in our control plane; we document what is stored.
2) KMS custody model: For Private/on-prem, PanMed may hold keys in your KMS/HSM. For hosted, we can integrate with PanMed-managed KMS keys (no plaintext key export).

I quoted a couple of lines from your sheet inline where we needed more detail — see the 'Notes' tab in the attached mapping.

Attaching: DPF_Mapping_By_Redwood.xlsx

If helpful, we can hop on a 30-minute call to walk the mapping.

Regards,
